newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Fogade sold $689 mln in assets in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Fogade sold $689 mln in assets in 1996.

text.p: Venezuela's State Deposits Guarantee Fund (Fogade) said it obtained $689.3 million from the sale this year of assets it inherited during the country's 1994-5 financial sector crisis.
Fogade said in data released to the press that it completed 12 of the 16 auctions that were planned in 1996.
The largest one was last week's sale of leading bank Banco de Venezuela to Spain's Banco Santander
That sale earned the Venezuelan state $376.38 million while the auction of Banco Consolidado , also last week, to Chilean financial group Infisau brought $154.38 million.
Among the companies Fogade failed to auction successfully this year, aluminum firm Alucasa is slated to go on sale at the beginning of 1997. Its latest base price was $40 million.
Other main privatizations due to take place next year include Banco Latino and Banco Republica.
Fogade received a large portfolio of assets in return for financial aid in the severe banking crisis that cost an estimated $11 billion in state bailouts.
